# Iteration 1 Report

## What Changed
- Slot A (`chinese_bigram_confusion_memory`): replaced ASCII-only tokenizer with Chinese
  character bigrams + ASCII tokens. Confusion matrix + disambiguation retrieval unchanged.
- Slot B (`reflexion_lesson_memory`): replaced raw example storage with LLM-distilled
  correction rules in a rule bank, retrieved by keyword fingerprint overlap.

## Results
- `chinese_bigram_confusion_memory`: 38/100 (+12 vs 26/100 baseline). New frontier.
- `reflexion_lesson_memory`: 23/100 (-3 vs baseline). Regressed.

## Why A Improved
The ASCII-only tokenizer produced near-zero Jaccard for all Chinese pairs, making retrieval
random. Bigrams restore meaningful similarity so topically similar cases rank higher. The
full +12 gain traces to this single fix.

## Why B Regressed
LLM-generated rules add noise and lose the concrete grounding of raw examples. Keyword
fingerprints are brittle for Chinese vocabulary. Cold-start performance was also worse
because rule generation requires prior errors before it contributes.

## Remaining Error Modes (score + feedback traces)
1. Label suffix hallucination: predicting "故意毁坏财物罪" when target is "故意毁坏财物" (~8 cases)
2. Wrong specificity: "受贿" vs "非国家工作人员受贿", "挪用公款" vs "挪用资金" (~8 cases)
3. Missing secondary charge: "故意伤害" alone vs "故意伤害;聚众哄抢" (~10 cases)
4. Wrong crime category: "盗窃" vs "破坏电力设备", "非法采矿" vs "非法占用农用地" (~8 cases)
5. Label format variants: "强迫他人吸食毒品" vs "强迫他人吸毒" (~4 cases)

## Takeaway
Bigram retrieval is now a solid base. The main remaining gap is that the LLM invents
approximate label strings rather than exact canonical ones. Iteration 2 should ground the
LLM in the exact labels observed in training (label vocabulary injection) and/or present
explicit contrastive corrections showing wrong→right label pairs for similar cases.
